elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted § 5.4: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL", with "Customer" expressly defined for that Section as IBM. The element is disjunctive (Agreement or Order Form), so Agreement-level coverage suffices; IBM's separate PO cancellation right in § 6.1 is preserved and unaffected.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL" — exactly 30 days, in writing, and no additional conditions (no consent, no minimum service period, no fee) are attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "MSL shall refund to Customer, on a pro rata basis, any fees prepaid by Customer for the period after the effective date of termination." The refund is expressly pro rata (not merely post-termination-period), runs from Vendor to Customer, and is triggered by the convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The three-year term "shall continue for a period of three (3) years unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0", and § 5.0/5.1 permits termination "by either Party for cause" only. The six-month notice in the term clause operates on the automatic twelve-month renewals ("will automatically be renewed ... unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice"), i.e. natural-term non-renewal assessed under RENEWAL, not a mid-term Vendor convenience exit. The new § 5.4 grants the convenience right to Customer only.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty (30) days' notice, which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band (and is more favourable to Customer, consistent with the preferred position being targeted).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed by the new § 5.4, but the retained termination-consequence text ("The price for Parts, whether in inventory or on order to meet IBM's forecasted requirements, shall be an amount equal to MSL's cost") plus § 6.1's preserved "cost reimbursements under the Price section" create an unquantified on-termination payment exposure; on the record supplied it cannot be confirmed to sit within three months' fees.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: MSL has no express convenience right during the committed term, but the only notice mechanic available to it ("unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement") does not expressly tie the effective date of termination to the end of the then-current renewal period, so it cannot be scored as term-end-only under the auto-renewal boundary.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The only Vendor notice mechanic requires six (6) months' written notice, which exceeds the 90-day minimum.

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the operative text: the single inserted § 5.4 supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day written notice, and the express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and the Vendor-side element is already met because § 5.0 confines MSL to for-cause termination during the three-year committed term (the six-month notice is a renewal-blocking mechanic properly assessed under RENEWAL).

Fallback is not satisfied (30 days sits outside the 60–90 day band and the Vendor notice right is not expressly term-end-effective), but that is irrelevant because the redline targets and completes the preferred level.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion, no "in whole or in part" surplus (no Order Form/partial-termination structure requires it), no survival tail, no fee cap, no added procedures, and no deletion or paraphrase of existing language — including the Customer-favourable § 6.1 PO cancellation right and the for-cause provisions, which are retained verbatim.

The one-sentence "For purposes of this Section 5.4, 'Customer' means IBM" is necessary rather than extra: "Customer" is otherwise undefined in this IBM/MSL agreement (the SOW uses "IBM Customer Order" for IBM's own customers), so omitting it would leave an undefined term and fail the intent test.

Intent is preserved: the new right is located within Section 5, matching the term clause's cross-reference "unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0"; the for-cause mechanics, inventory/parts cost provisions, PO cancellation right and cost-reimbursement carve-outs all survive without contradiction, and no cross-reference is left dangling.

Optional hardening (not required for completeness): if the retained parts/inventory cost-reimbursement obligations could be triggered by a § 5.4 convenience exit, consider a short carve-out or cap so the exit is genuinely "without penalty"; and if MSL's six-month renewal notice is ever read as a mid-term exit, add "effective at the end of the then-current term" to that sentence.
